taxonomy.note: Older nursery, horticultural, and Texas references frequently use Conoclinium greggii.

project_tracker_diagnostic: Rhizomatous perennial with ovate-deltate leaves that are deeply lobed/dissected, and fuzzy lavender-blue to purple discoid flower heads.

project_inclusion.learning_reason: Very useful Central Texas mistflower and an important current-name/synonym lesson.

morphology_keys.habit: Erect to spreading perennial, often arising from knotty crowns and capable of forming colonies.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite; blades ovate-deltate to ovate, roughly 1.5–4 cm, with margins distinctly lobed or dissected.
morphology_keys.heads: Small discoid heads; florets lavender-blue to purple, without ray florets.
morphology_keys.phyllaries: About 3.5–5 mm in Flora of North America.
morphology_keys.fruit: Cypselae about 1.8–2.5 mm with a bristly pappus.

photo_strategy.selection_logic: Use accepted iNaturalist taxon Conoclinium dissectum; prefer curated references plus several views from one Central Texas/Texas observation.
